facts.fact: An INASA presentation given in Bissau on 26 January 2019 states that Guinea-Bissau, through INASA, has used the DHIS2 platform for the management of health information since mid-2011, with SIS officers at regional and health-area level in its information flow.

INASA says that after its decision to take DHIS2 beyond the tuberculosis programme, the monthly reports of malaria, health centres and hospitals, the weekly epidemiological surveillance reports and the HIV/AIDS data sets began to be captured online at gbsis.dhis2.org; the slide is undated, so the presentation's date is used, and it does not distinguish levels of hospital.
INASA lists among targets reached in 2017 the implementation of data recording in all 11 health regions.

INASA reports that Real Time Monitoring entered a pilot phase in 2018: data entry at health-area level on tablets over the mobile phone network, directly from the health areas, with the entry process monitored.

INASA describes tablet data entry from the health areas (RTM) as in its pilot phase in 2018, gives no number of pilot health areas, and recommends in January 2019 that RTM be expanded to all health areas.
